Proposition
[Uniqueness of the submersion metric]

↗ lem:riemannian-submersion-inner-eq

For a Riemannian metric $\tilde g$ on $\tilde M$ and a surjective smooth submersion $\pi :\tilde M\to M$, at most one metric on $M$ makes $\pi $ a Riemannian submersion.

Proof

↗ lem:riemannian-submersion-inner-eq \sketch If $g_1,g_2$ both work and $y=\pi (x)$, Lemma 3 gives $(g_1)_y=\beta _x=(g_2)_y$.

□

For a smooth action of a group $G$ on $\tilde M$, call it vertical when $\pi (a\cdot x)=\pi (x)$, transitive on fibers when any two points in one fiber differ by an element of $G$, and isometric when each action map preserves $\tilde g$.
